ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Preventive Visit — Elvis Presley — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mr. Presley is a 39-year-old singer with opioid use disorder on buprenorphine, a benzodiazepine use disorder on a slow diazepam taper, stage 2 hypertension, obesity with prediabetes, obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP, opioid-induced constipation and glaucoma, who comes for his yearly preventive visit one week after his three-week review and five days before a Las Vegas engagement. He has taken buprenorphine 16 mg every morning without withdrawal and with few cravings. He took the first diazepam step, to 36 mg a day, a week ago and noticed only slightly worse sleep for two nights. He took his first tirzepatide dose a week ago and had mild nausea for a day. He uses CPAP most nights and feels more awake in the afternoon. His bowels open every one to two days. He has not had a tetanus booster in more than ten years and has never been tested for HIV or hepatitis. [S]

Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan updated. Lipids: total cholesterol 214, HDL 38, LDL 140 and triglycerides 180 mg/dL, a pattern that fits obesity and prediabetes. At 39 the pooled cohort equations do not apply; his 10-year risk by the AHA PREVENT equations is low, so a statin is not indicated now, and weight loss, activity and blood pressure control are the main steps. [S]
Repeat lipids after six months of weight treatment.
HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B tests drawn today.
Next preventive visit in one year.

Weekly video visits while he is away.

Follow-up: Las Vegas engagement with weekly video visits; ten-week review after he returns. HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B results by phone. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1974-09-23: ten-week review after the Las Vegas engagement and a back strain: buprenorphine, the taper, weight treatment, sleep apnea and planning for a three-week tour. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent, a long-time friend who works with him, and a health care proxy form was completed; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is being able to sing and to be there for the people who depend on him, and that he would want full treatment, including resuscitation and breathing support, after an overdose or other sudden illness. The plan will be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
